title: Connected Double Slabs By Blond
description: Making the double slab block useful with CTM!
body:
![The cover image for the resource pack, featuring a bunch of connected double slabs.](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/4c60cfd37722547fc95621bb8f66e004706abde8.png)

Take two slabs, stack them on top of each other, and you get a double slab block which looks identical to a full block. Well, what if it wasn't? This resource pack takes every double slab block in the game and gives them unique textures for both building and distinguishability!

### Compatibility
If you just want the ability to tell full blocks and double slabs apart, this pack fully achieves that as a standalone resource pack without any mods, but it also works with any mod that uses either uses the **McPatcher CTM** format or the **Fusion CTM** format. (Yea it works with both lol [' > ,])
- [Continuity](https://modrinth.com/mod/continuity) and [OptiFine](https://optifine.net/home) support the **McPatcher CTM** format.
- [Fusion](https://modrinth.com/mod/fusion-connected-textures) supports the **Fusion CTM** format.
- I didn't know ConnectedTexturesMod, ya know, the mod called "CTM", doesn't use the classic McPatcher CTM format. I'll look into adding support for it at some point in the future.

In theory, this pack should be able to work alongside any standard CTM pack, but just in case I've developed my own CTM pack called [Connected Textures By Blond]([https://modrinth.com/resourcepack/connected-double-slabs-by-blond](https://modrinth.com/resourcepack/connected-textures-by-blond)). Both packs were made simultaneously and even share a few textures! **Just make sure the double slab pack is above the ctm one in the resource packs menu!**

### Special Thanks
**MASSIVE** shoutout to my best friend for making a program to help create the texture files needed for all of this to work. This whole thing *would* have been possible without Jake's help, but *man* it would've been slow and painful.

The tool is [here](https://github.com/JakeThe28th/ctm_tool) if you want to check it out and use it yourself!
